correctness.rationale: The three row subcomplexes are S^(n-2) by the nerve theorem. Their pairwise intersections are crown graphs plus n isolated third-row vertices, and the triple intersection is the discrete 3n vertices. In the integral three-cover Mayer-Vietoris double complex the triple-to-pair map projects onto a signed 3n-by-3n permutation matrix on isolated coordinates, proving saturated rank 3n. The component-to-single-cover map has rank 2, and the three pairwise crown cycle lattices have rank n^2-3n+1 each. Therefore H_1=Z, H_2=Z^(3n^2-9n+3), H_(n-2)=Z^3 and other reduced groups vanish, with no torsion. The checker independently enumerates all faces and mod-two ranks n=5..8; finite checks are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The closest all-parameter rook-neighborhood classification explicitly leaves low-dimensional integral homology unknown; the present three-row family computes it completely with a substantive new triple-overlap calculation. The quadratic number of 2-cycles, unique integral 1-cycle and uniform torsion-free behavior characterize an infinite natural line-graph family and distinguish its low-dimensional topology from the 4-by-4 torsion-bearing case. It is neither a simple parameter substitution from two rows nor merely a finite example.
